title: John Stuart Mill's birth chart
metaDescription: John Stuart Mill's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 28.7° Taurus. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: 0.2° separates Mars and Jupiter from an exact trine; at that range drive and expansion read as one mechanism. The scheme reads trines as water finding its level: effortless, and invisible to the person living it.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: At noon on that date the Sun stood at 28.7° Taurus, inside the third decan (20°–30°), whose traditional sub-ruler is Saturn. The decan is the older, finer division — it is what the sign looks like once you stop rounding it to thirty degrees.

blocks.title: The personal registers
blocks.text: For the fast movers, Mercury was at 5.5° Taurus, Venus was at 12.9° Aries, Mars was at 7.1° Taurus. Read together: thought with its feet on the ground; attraction declared rather than implied; effort banked steadily until it tells.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: The day's firmest angle joins Mars and Jupiter — a trine holding at 0.2°. The scheme reads trines as water finding its level: effortless, and invisible to the person living it. Behind it, the Sun opposition Neptune at 0.2°, and Saturn conjunction Uranus at 0.5° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. The unknown hour cannot unmake any of this: every aspect named survived all twenty-five samples of the day.

blocks.title: Figures in the geometry
blocks.text: The Moon makes no major aspect that survives the day; the old reading gives such a planet autonomy — it acts alone, sometimes loudly.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The oldest layer of the scheme — seven planets, four conditions — flags four placements in this chart. Venus in Aries at 12.9° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; Mars in Taurus at 7.1° is in detriment; Jupiter in Capricorn at 7.3° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given; Saturn in Libra at 22.7° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best. Dignity is a statement about conditions, not about worth.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Among the 9 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, the elements divide 4 earth, 2 air, 2 water, 1 fire; by modality, 4 fixed, 4 cardinal, 1 mutable. Earth weights a chart toward the material and the durable — what can be built, kept, and relied on. Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune were retrograde — motion that reverses only from this vantage point, and which the old reading treats as delay used for revision.

blocks.title: The Moon is genuinely open
blocks.text: The Moon crossed from Gemini into Cancer during that day at the birthplace, travelling 14.4° between one midnight and the next. The hour would decide it; no hour was recorded. The reading keeps the question open rather than flipping a coin dressed as astrology.
